activity_context.topic_title: Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes of Rational Functions

feedback.worked_solution:
For large positive values of $x,$ we have $|6x-2|=6x-2.$ Consequently, for $x\to \infty ,$ we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{|6x-2|}{8x+5}={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{6x-2}{8x+5}.
$$

First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{1}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{6x-2}{8x+5} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{6x}{x}-\frac{2}{x})}{(\frac{8x}{x}+\frac{5}{x})} \\  & {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(6-\frac{2}{x})}{(8+\frac{5}{x})} \\  & =\frac{6-0}{8-0} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
